document_title: Alaska's AI budget order changes hands December 7th.

slides.headline: Alaska's AI budget order changes hands December 7th.
Every agency is told to follow the money with AI.
slides.body: Signed August 4th, 2025. The Office of Management and Budget runs the review every year.
labels: "Utilize technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to review large datasets in order to determine how State of Alaska funds are actually being spent."

slides.headline: One office runs it. It reaches every agency.
slides.body: The order makes the Office of Management and Budget responsible. It applies to the executive branch, including departments, boards, commissions and public corporations.

slides.headline: Seven duties. Two of them are AI.
labels: Use AI to review large datasets
Recommend where AI can realize efficiencies
FIRST FOCUS · GRANTS TO NON-STATE ENTITIES · ACCOUNTS PAYABLE
OMB MUST PUBLISH A YEARLY LIST OF FUNDS GRANTED

slides.headline: It said reserves would cover seven months.
slides.body: The order said state savings could fund only seven months of government operations, and that no process existed to review zero base budget spending. Dunleavy said it would "eliminate waste."
labels: ASH BAND · THE ORDER'S STATED REASONS

slides.headline: It took effect immediately. It runs until revoked.
The office it names gets a new head.
slides.body: Governor-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins named Alexei Painter to lead the Office of Management and Budget. Painter is leaving the Legislature, where he helped guide lawmakers' budget process. He once worked as an OMB analyst.

slides.headline: On December 7th, the order passes on.
slides.body: Kreiss-Tomkins takes office December 7th. The order stays in effect until revoked, so keeping it, rewriting it or revoking it becomes his call.

slides.headline: Should every agency keep reading the budget with AI?

post_copy:
Alaska's order telling every agency to review spending with AI has no end date. A new governor inherits it on December 7th.

Leaving it alone is a decision too.

Mike Dunleavy signed Administrative Order 359 on August 4th, 2025.
Every agency is told to use AI to see how state funds "are actually being spent."
Two of its seven agency duties name AI.
Grants to non-state entities and accounts payable are the first focus areas.
The order puts the Office of Management and Budget in charge.
On November 18th Governor-elect Kreiss-Tomkins named Alexei Painter to lead that office.

Swipe for the AI clause word for word, the order's seven duties and its own 2025 case, then the new budget director and the December 7th handoff.

Should a standing AI order over the budget stay one governor's call, or should the Legislature get a say?

#AlaskaBudget #PublicSectorAI #AlaskaPolitics

editor_notes_for_email: Slide copy carried from the storyboard unchanged. The post copy is the room's winning caption byte for byte, hashtag line included, and the website link appears only in the first comment. Whether OMB ever published the AO 359 yearly grants list or any Government Efficiency Review output is UNVERIFIED either way, because omb.alaska.gov returned 503 on both tries; slide 04 states the duty to publish and nothing more. Linking Alexei Painter to AO 359 is the deck's own inference, from the order naming OMB as responsible (S36) and ADN reporting that Painter will lead OMB (C20); ADN never mentions AI or AO 359, so slide 07 says only what each source says. The order's reserves and no-process lines on slide 05 are attributed to the order as its own August 2025 case. This session ran at effort medium, not the high the repo's settings file carries.
